A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, and experiments. All 12 pages of each PDF were inspected, including figures, tables, and equations. Both end with references; neither contains the separately referenced supplementary sections A/B, so those unavailable sections are outside this comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generated examples, a 95-participant preference study, CLIP scores, baseline comparisons, and component ablations in Section 6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical comparisons and quantitative results and reports a Neural Template guidance ablation in Section 6.3.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains coarse dynamic geometry, consistency-model refinement, DINOv2 Neural State Maps, the hybrid K-Planes/NGP representation, physically based rendering, and the same distillation objectives. Sections 5.1–5.2 explain the existing signed-distance representation and rendering more explicitly without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven processes: flower blooming, flower withering, plant sprouting, candle burning, ice cream melting, banana rotting, and bread baking. The replacement guidance ablation uses the already represented rose scenario.

E2.justification: DreamGaussian4D, 4D-fy, STAG4D, and Fantasia3D remain the main baselines. Within the ablation comparisons, v1's Figure 8 includes frame-by-frame 3D reconstruction and no-ARAP/no-flow variants; these disappear from v2, which instead evaluates generation without Neural Template guidance.

E3.justification: The seven-process evaluation, 95-participant preference study, three preference criteria, and CLIP metric remain unchanged. The local ablation design changes: v2 disables Neural Template guidance and displays three frames from two viewpoints, replacing the mesh-construction controls in v1's Figure 8.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 replaces the coarse-mesh analysis of ARAP, flow supervision, and framewise reconstruction with an analysis of whether Neural Template guidance prevents inconsistent views and weak motion. The consistency-refinement and representation ablations are retained, renumbered from Figures 9–10 to Figures 8–9.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same aggregate preference percentages and CLIP scores. Neither supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All Table 1 values remain identical, including the proposed method's preference percentages of 76.84%, 69.77%, and 61.05%, and CLIP score of 30.83. v2 adds qualitative unguided-generation failures and removes the coarse-mesh ablation results. Figure 6 also revises the displayed 4D-fy sprouting examples, without establishing a performance change under matched conditions.

T1.justification: The Neural Template mapping, Equations 1–5, and video regularization loss retain their mathematical content. Describing the existing signed-distance representation as a time-evolving implicit level set adds explanation, not a new formal definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: temporal object-intrinsics generation from 2D foundation models, Neural Template guidance, a hybrid 4D representation, and controllable rendering. The new ablation supplies support without changing these claims.

C2.justification: v1's ablation discussion explains how flow supervision improves deformation gradients and why framewise reconstruction fails on back views; this discussion is removed. v2 instead interprets cross-view artifacts and tiny motion without Neural Template guidance as evidence of its necessity. The other principal interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly describes differentiable volume rendering of per-coordinate shading into frames and concatenating those frames into a video. Section 5.1 also makes the existing implicit signed-distance representation more explicit. These are documentation additions; no changed hardware, training budget, hyperparameters, or resource-access information is reported.

R1.justification: v2 adds three references supporting the implicit-surface explanation: Mehta et al.'s level-set theory, Novello et al.'s neural implicit surface evolution, and NeuS2. The related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning otherwise remain the same after matching renumbered citations.

P1.justification: Localized edits simplify the system overview, rename Section 4.1, explicitly name DINOv2, expand Sections 5.1–5.2, and introduce shading and volume-rendering subheadings. The acknowledgments add the artistic inspiration for the title. The overall section structure and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from a full-width display to a much smaller single-column display. Several figures are reduced or repositioned; Figure 6 revises sprouting examples, and Figure 4 updates its mesh label. The removed mesh-ablation figure is replaced by a guidance-ablation figure, while retained analyses are renumbered and rearranged.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the representation and rendering workflow and adds direct evidence about the central Neural Template guidance mechanism. However, it removes useful evidence about coarse-mesh construction, and the compressed Table 1 is less readable. With the main quantitative evidence unchanged, these concrete gains and losses do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
